title: Hierarchical KV memory partitioning with cross-plane sync to reduce multi-GPU KV footprint and variance
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: In tensor/pipeline parallel configurations we observe a large per-GPU KV cache duplication and high tail-latency variance when continuous batching drives many large prefix requests. Current approaches replicate KV entries across tensor-parallel ranks or apply coarse-grained striping which leads to wasted memory and uneven eviction hotspots.

Goal: Design and implement a hierarchical KV memory partitioning system with light-weight cross-plane synchronization and epochal resharding to reduce overall GPU KV footprint by >=35% for common LLM workloads, while keeping 99th percentile token latency regression under 5% vs baseline. The design should coordinate tensor and pipeline parallel boundaries, be compatible with existing KV cache APIs, and allow gradual rollout with canary monitors.

Scope: algorithm and runtime changes to allocation + eviction, cross-plane metadata syncing, a per-GPU local slab + global segment index, integration with continuous batching/backpressure, and metrics/alerts for evictions and reshard events. Out of scope: model graph rewrites and changes to model checkpoint format.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end integration tests for TPxPP topologies (2x1, 4x2) pass in CI
Real workload benchmarks show >=35% reduction in aggregate KV GPU memory across a suite of 7 curated prompts (chat, long-context summarization, code completion)
99th percentile token latency increases by <=5% on median hardware (A100-80GB class) under production continuous-batch load
No correctness regressions: generation outputs identical to baseline for deterministic evals and within existing fuzz tolerances for non-deterministic models
Graceful fallback enabled: if cross-plane sync fails, system reverts to per-GPU replicated cache with metrics indicating fallback reason
technical_notes:
Core idea: split KV address space into hierarchical segments: a small global index (segment directory) that is synchronized across tensor-parallel ranks in a lightweight, incremental fashion; per-GPU local slabs hold the actual KV storage for segments assigned to that rank. During inference a mapping lookup uses the segment directory to decide whether to access local slab, request a remote fetch, or use a shared read-only window.

Key components:
- Segment Directory: compact versioned map of segment -> owning rank(s) + sequence range + hotness score. Small enough to be replicated to all ranks and updated at epoch boundaries.
- Local Slabs: per-GPU allocators optimized for continuous-batching fragmentation (power-of-two bins + prefix coalescing for contiguous KV blobs).
- Cross-plane Sync: epochal commit protocol that uses a single producer ring and delta patches (no global barrier) to update the directory; uses sequence numbers to detect lost patches and triggers safe fallback reshard.
- Eviction Policy: hotspot-aware cooperative eviction: when hotness exceeds threshold we spread segment replicas across adjacent pipeline ranks rather than full replication to limit duplication.
- Backpressure integration: when remote fetch latency or memory pressure rises we reduce batch concurrency for affected routes and prefetch the next likely segment based on prefix heuristics.

Implementation notes: incremental implementation as a runtime flag (kv_partitioning_v1). Start with read-only segment directory and local slab allocators; then enable delta patches; finally enable dynamic replica placement. Use mmap-friendly structures to allow zero-copy when moving segments between ranks for on-prem deployments.
decisions: Avoid full global barrier for reshard; prefer epochal delta patches to minimize inference pauses
Use per-GPU local slabs with a compact global directory rather than fully-distributed hash to reduce metadata churn
Replica placement will be topology-aware (co-locate replicas on pipeline neighbors) to reduce cross-host traffic
Fallback strategy: if directory patching fails for more than 2 epochs, revert to per-GPU replicated cache and emit a high-severity alert
updates: 2026-02-22: Spike completed comparing power-of-two slab bins vs buddy allocator; chosen power-of-two with prefix coalescing for lower fragmentation (Aisha)
2026-02-28: Microbenchmarks show local slab allocation throughput within 5% of baseline, fragmentation reduced by ~18% for long-context workloads (Marco)
2026-03-04: Design review with Runtime & Infra teams; main feedback to add safe fallback and to quantify directory size limits for 8k context models (reviewed by Priya Shah)

2026-03-09: Prototype of segment directory delta patching implemented in runtime branch feat/kv-hier-part; initial end-to-end test on 2x1 topology passes smoke checks (PR: github.com/redwood-repo/runtime/pull/2153)
2026-03-12: Load test scheduled against benchmark cluster; observed early memory reduction ~28% on mixed prompt set, investigating variance on heavy code-completion workloads (Marco)
test_plan: Unit tests for directory encoding/decoding, integration tests for three topologies (1x1, 2x1 TPxPP, 4x2 TPxPP), fuzz tests for patch loss and reshard fallback, regression tests against generation outputs. Performance: run benchmark harness with continuous batching at 2x, 5x, and 10x baseline concurrency to measure memory, throughput, and p99 latency. Add synthetic test that simulates rapid hot-segment churn to validate eviction spread logic.
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind kv_partitioning_v1. Rollout steps: 1) Internal staging cluster (smoke & perf) 2) Canary on small customer-facing cluster with telemetry for evictions, directory patch loss, and fallback counts 3) Gradual ramp to 25% traffic with automatic rollback on >2% customers triggered fallback or >5% p99 latency regression 4) Full rollout. Add alerting: KV:partitioning:fallback_count and KV:partitioning:dir_size. Post-rollout review after 2 weeks.
